questions.question: According to CSS naming conventions, which of the following is the correct way to name a CSS file?
questions.explanation: CSS files should use lowercase letters, no spaces, and avoid special characters. Dashes and underscores are acceptable, so 'my-styles.css' is correct.

questions.question: What is the correct file extension for CSS files?
questions.explanation: All CSS files must have the .css file extension.

questions.question:
Consider this CSS rule:
```css
h1 { color: blue; font-size: 12px; }
```

What is the 'selector' in this rule?
questions.explanation: The selector is 'h1' - it's the pattern used to select the element(s) you want to style. Selectors come before the curly braces.

questions.question:
Consider this CSS rule:
```css
h1 { color: blue; font-size: 12px; }
```

What is a 'declaration' in this rule?
questions.explanation: A declaration is any single property/value specification. 'color: blue;' is one declaration, and 'font-size: 12px;' is another. Each declaration ends with a semicolon.

questions.question:
Consider this CSS rule:
```css
h1 { color: blue; font-size: 12px; }
```

What is the 'property' in the first declaration?
questions.explanation: The property is 'color' - it refers to what you want to change. Properties come before the colon in a declaration.

questions.question:
Consider this CSS rule:
```css
h1 { color: blue; font-size: 12px; }
```

What is the 'value' in the first declaration?
questions.explanation: The value is 'blue' - it refers to how you want to change the property. Values come after the colon in a declaration.

questions.question: Which of the following is the recommended way to include CSS in an HTML document?
questions.explanation: External style sheets (using a <link> tag in the <head>) are recommended. Internal style sheets are only for testing/convenience, and inline styles are not recommended.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for linking an external CSS file?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax is: <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="mystyle.css">. This should be placed inside the <head> tag.

questions.question: What happens if you forget the semicolon after a CSS declaration?
options: Your whole style sheet will break
questions.explanation: If you forget to put the semicolon after each style declaration, your whole style sheet will break. Semicolons are required to separate declarations.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct CSS syntax?
questions.explanation: Correct CSS syntax uses curly braces { } around declarations, colons : between properties and values, and semicolons ; after each declaration.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for CSS comments?
questions.explanation: CSS comments use the syntax /* comment */. Comments are useful for organizing and documenting your styles.

questions.question: What does 'specificity' mean in CSS?
options: The means by which browsers decide which CSS property values are the most relevant to an element
How many properties you can use
questions.explanation: Specificity is the means by which browsers decide which CSS property values are the most relevant to an element and, therefore, will be applied. More specific rules take precedence.

questions.question: According to the cascade rules, what happens if two CSS rules have the same specificity?
options: The more recent rule takes precedence
questions.explanation: If two rules share the same specificity, then the more 'recent' rule takes precedence. This is part of how the CSS cascade works.

questions.question: What is the cascade in CSS?
options: The way that CSS styles are applied to HTML elements, where styles cascade down to descendants unless overridden
questions.explanation: The 'cascade' refers to the way that CSS styles are applied to HTML elements. Styles applied to elements cascade down to their descendants, unless they are overridden.

questions.question: Can you use multiple CSS files in a single HTML document?
options: No, only one CSS file is allowed
Yes, you can use as many CSS files as you want by including multiple <link> tags
Yes, but only if they're in the same directory
Yes, but only external files, not internal styles
questions.explanation: You can use as many CSS files as you want. This is useful for organizing code and taking advantage of third-party style sheets. Just include multiple <link> tags in the <head>.

questions.question: Which of the following should NEVER appear in a CSS file?
questions.explanation: CSS files should never have HTML tags inside of them. No angle brackets <> in a style sheet, ever. CSS files contain only CSS rules, not HTML.
